about: The independent checker's reply, as it came back (a Sonnet agent given the guide's text by section and the 68 situations with the sections each key already listed; A = the 38 turn-130 situations, B = the 30 held-out ones). Fable checked every quote in the text. Additions were applied (EXPECTED-REVIEWED.json, SITUATIONS-HELDOUT.json); of its removals only S059 from B17 was applied.

add.quote: Many struggle to get past the silly, awkward feeling of it.
add.why: Names the same predicament of feeling silly doing inner-child work.

add.quote: It felt like I was making it up at first, which seems quite common.
add.why: Describes the made-up feeling and says to shift to listening and waiting.

add.quote: You don’t have to believe these words. Watch what I do.
add.why: Gives the reply to a little one who says they do not believe you.

add.quote: If a voice or urge is directing you towards harm, and you feel at risk of acting on it, as with myself and those ghosts at home, move away from that open window and get some outside support.
add.why: Direct advice for someone at risk of acting on a harmful urge.

add.quote: You call up the Nurturer and try to talk to your little one, and you get silence or a numb feeling, and all of a sudden your phone or the laundry feels urgent.
add.why: Describes getting nothing when trying to reach the little one.

remove.why: About getting mad or staring at the rug, not about nothing coming up.

add.quote: Be careful what you mix, too, and not just prescribed medicines.
add.why: Practical caution for someone planning to take psychedelics.

add.quote: And any predisposition toward mania or psychosis is a warning sign too, whether it’s family history, a bad environment or a bad mindset.
add.why: Risk screening a person should do before planning psychedelic use.

remove.why: About what to do after a trip that went badly, not about planning a first or new one.
Only a one-line intro to the conflict chapter, with no advice for hitting back.

add.quote: Notice how, when you offer thanks (to the universe, to life, to God, whatever you may believe in), a space in your heart opens up.
add.why: Gives a concrete place to start toward the bigger love.

remove.why: Reflects on joy in sorrow and does not say where to start.

add.quote: At this stage, use your childlike superpowers to come into the “Wow of Now” (have you seen the movie Waking Life?), and make sure there’s enough safety around you to continue with reparenting.
add.why: Tells someone not yet steady to build safety before continuing.

remove.why: About a part of you that came to the guide, not about readiness to dig into childhood.

add.quote: Whose approval suddenly feels like I can’t live without it?
add.why: Questions for the fear of what others think, including praise, blame and reputation.

add.quote: Say you had a spiritual opening years before you had much of a Nurturer or Protector.
add.why: Addresses spiritual freedom that has not reached the little one.

add.quote: You can have an enormous spiritual feast upstairs while the child is still starving downstairs.
add.why: Same predicament of feeling free while the child inside is still hurting.

remove.why: General chicken-and-egg discussion that does not address meditation freedom or being called lazy.

add.why: Tells how to borrow a friend's way of sitting with you when you fall apart.

add.quote: When you take turns listening with a good peer, on an equal footing, their warmth and the way they hold space for you are ideal for borrowing the Nurturer role and what that feels like.
add.why: A friend or peer doing part of the grown-up role first.

add.quote: Are you really sorry for what you did, or are you just trying to feel sorry because they’re upset?
add.why: Advice on repair and on guilt that keeps shouting after you hurt someone.

remove.why: About not over-relying on an outer adult, not about a teacher's betrayal or meditation feeling tainted.
About starting a session with whatever shows up, not about closing one.

add.quote: So if it feels like you’re enforcing everything as a discipline, see if you can change that discipline into a game.
add.why: Directly addresses a healthy routine like yoga feeling like enforced discipline.

add.quote: So if it feels like you’re enforcing everything as a discipline, see if you can change that discipline into a game.
add.why: Addresses practice that has turned into an enforced duty.
